the only stage byte reduction touches
68.1% of the gate. Picks 6 of 64 values per layer and costs MORE than the shared experts, which do 130x the arithmetic. Pure dispatch.

REFUTED_HYPOTHESIS: The router computes `x @ self.weight.T` per call, per layer, per token, so a per-call transpose looked like free waste. Pre-transposing to a contiguous [2048,64] saves -0.0037 ms -- indistinguishable from zero. MLX resolves the transpose as a view. Not a lever.
WHERE_THE_ROUTER_COST_ACTUALLY_IS: Selection, not projection. 0.724 of the gate's 1.063 ms. For top-6-of-64 on ONE token that is sigmoid + bias-add + argpartition + take_along_axis + sum + divide + scale, roughly 7 launches x 26 layers = ~180 dispatches for arithmetic that would fit in a single small kernel. It is already @mx.compile'd, so the remaining cost is launch, not Python.
DEAD_CODE_FOUND: n_group=1 on this specimen, so the entire group-limited routing branch of group_expert_select (unflatten/topk/argpartition/put_along_axis/flatten) never executes. Any fused replacement only has to implement the n_group==1 path.
HONEST_STATUS: The dominant stage is LOCATED and RANKED by direct isolation, and one candidate fix was tested and refuted. The remaining fixes -- a fused router-select kernel (~0.7 ms, 8%) or an MLA rewrite (~3.5 ms, 40%) -- both require writing Metal, which is a build, not a measurement. G017 asks for both halves and only the first is done.
